title_tag: 从贫民窟女孩到诺贝尔和平奖！今年诺贝尔和平奖得主到底是什么来头？—— 美国纽约时报外刊讲解第1195天
h1: 从贫民窟女孩到诺贝尔和平奖！今年诺贝尔和平奖得主到底是什么来头？
category: 美国纽约时报外刊讲解 第1195天
nav_hint: An International Career Forged by the Struggles of Apartheid

headline.en_html: An International Career Forged by the Struggles of Apartheid — Navi Pillay, who won this year’s Nobel Peace Prize, fought racism in South Africa, shaping her international career as a judge and advocate for justice and human rights.
headline.zh: 一段国际职业生涯，由种族隔离的斗争锻造而成——纳维·皮莱，今年的诺贝尔和平奖得主；她曾在南非与种族主义抗争，正是这段经历，塑造了她作为法官、作为正义与人权倡导者的国际生涯。

notes.en: A career is a job or profession that someone does for a long time.
notes.zh: 职业，事业（一整条职业轨道）
notes.ctx: 标题里她的生涯不是“找到”的，而是一整条被锤打出来的职业轨道，与 job 的临时性正相反。
notes.ex1: She has had a distinguished career in international law. 她在国际法领域拥有辉煌的职业生涯。
notes.ex2: He switched careers at the age of forty. 他四十岁那年转换了职业轨道。

notes.en: To forge means to make an object from metal by heating and hammering it; figuratively, to create something strong and lasting with great effort.
notes.zh: 锻造；（引申）千锤百炼地打造
notes.ctx: 标题的灵魂动词：本义铁匠铺里烧红锤打，本文指被苦难反复敲打出来的东西，比 build 多了烈火与痛感。
notes.ex1: Their friendship was forged during years of hardship. 他们的友谊是在多年的患难中锻造出来的。
notes.ex2: The two countries forged a trade agreement. 两国缔结了一项贸易协定。

notes.en: Apartheid was a political system in which people of different races were separated and treated unequally.
notes.ctx: 南非 1948 至 1994 年的法定制度，按肤色划分居住、就学与公共设施，是全文所有苦难的总背景。
notes.ex1: She grew up under apartheid. 她在种族隔离制度下长大。
notes.ex2: Apartheid ended in 1994. 种族隔离制度于 1994 年终结。

notes.en: Racism is the belief that people of different races have different qualities, and unfair treatment of people based on race.
notes.ctx: 副标题用 racism 而不用 apartheid：制度可以废除，观念却未必随之消失，这是她斗了一辈子的东西。
notes.ex1: She fought racism her whole life. 她一生都在与种族主义抗争。
notes.ex2: The report exposed institutional racism. 报告揭露了制度性种族歧视。

notes.en: An advocate is a person who publicly supports a cause or policy; as a verb, to publicly support an idea.
notes.zh: 倡导者，拥护者；公开倡导
notes.ctx: 词根 voc 是“喊”：她不只是坐在法庭上的法官，还是站在前头替正义大声疾呼的人。
notes.ex1: She is a lifelong advocate for justice. 她是一生为正义奔走呼吁的人。
notes.ex2: The group advocates peaceful protest. 该组织倡导和平抗议。

notes.en: Justice is fairness in the way people are treated, and the legal system of a country.
notes.ctx: 全文的题眼：judge 是她的职业，justice 是她一生追的东西，结尾那句 keep going, seeking justice 正是落点。
notes.ex1: She spent her life seeking justice. 她一生都在寻求正义。
notes.ex2: The criminals were finally brought to justice. 罪犯终于被绳之以法。

paragraphs.en_html: She lived her childhood in a <mark class="voc">slum</mark> without <mark class="voc">sewage</mark> or water, attended a school for only children of Indian <mark class="voc">descent</mark>, and knew that her skin color <mark class="voc">prohibited</mark> her from going to the beach her father would drive past during the Christmas season.
paragraphs.zh: 她的童年，安放在一个没有下水道、没有自来水的贫民窟里；她就读的，是一所只向印度裔孩子开放的学校；而她打小就知道，自己的肤色是一道禁令——父亲每年圣诞节驱车经过的那片海滩，永远不许她踏足。

notes.en: A slum is an area of a city where many people live in very bad housing conditions with extreme poverty.
notes.ctx: 开篇第一个名词就把她放在最底层；slum 重“穷”，ghetto 重“特定族群被强制圈居”，两者不可混用。
notes.ex1: She spent her childhood in a slum. 她的童年在贫民窟度过。
notes.ex2: Millions of slum dwellers lack clean water. 数百万贫民窟居民用不上洁净水。

notes.en: Sewage is the mixture of waste and used water carried away from buildings by pipes.
notes.ctx: without sewage or water 两个名词写尽制度性贫困，作者不写“她很穷”，只甩细节，让读者自己得出结论。
notes.ex1: The slum had no sewage system. 贫民窟没有排污系统。
notes.ex2: Raw sewage flowed into the river. 未经处理的污水直接排入河中。

notes.en: Descent means a person's family origin or background; also the action of going down.
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义：of Indian descent 是有印度血统，比 Indians living abroad 更简洁；本义“下降”在本文不出现。
notes.ex1: She is of Indian descent. 她有印度血统。
notes.ex2: The plane began its descent. 飞机开始下降。

notes.en: To prohibit means to forbid by law or rule; to prevent someone from doing something.
notes.ctx: prohibited her from going to the beach：不是她不想去，是法律不许她去，一个词写尽制度之恶。
notes.ex1: The law prohibits discrimination. 法律禁止歧视。
notes.ex2: Smoking is prohibited in public places. 公共场所禁止吸烟。

paragraphs.en_html: But she also described a pivotal moment that helped her rise from <mark class="voc">under the thumb of</mark> racism: Parents in her community in the coastal city of Durban <mark class="voc">pooled</mark> their money to send her to university, after her high school principal said she had potential. That opportunity began a <mark class="voc">barrier-breaking</mark> career that led Ms. Pillay to becoming a lawyer, a judge on multiple international courts, the human rights chief of the United Nations and, on Friday, a Nobel Peace Prize <mark class="voc">laureate</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 但她也说起过自己命运的支点——那一刻，她得以从种族主义的压制之下起身：只因高中校长一句“这孩子有潜力”，德班这座滨海城市里，社区的家长们便你一份我一份地凑出钱来，送她进了大学。正是这个机会，开启了她一路破壁的职业生涯：律师、多个国际法庭的法官、联合国人权事务负责人，直到上周五——诺贝尔和平奖桂冠加身。

notes.en: Under the thumb of someone means completely controlled by them and unable to act freely.
notes.ctx: 画面是大拇指把人摁在底下；它与后半句的 rise from 正好对照——被摁住的和不肯停下的，是同一个人。
notes.ex1: For years she lived under the thumb of the system. 多年来她活在这个体制的压制之下。
notes.ex2: He refused to stay under the thumb of his boss. 他不肯再受老板的摆布。

notes.en: To pool money or resources means to combine them so they can be used more effectively.
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义：本义是“共同的水塘”，大家把钱倒进一个池子，谁需要谁取用——社区的家长就是这样凑出她的学费。
notes.ex1: The parents pooled their money to hire a teacher. 家长们凑钱请了一位老师。
notes.ex2: We pooled our ideas to solve the problem. 我们集思广益解决这个问题。

notes.en: Barrier-breaking describes something that breaks down barriers and removes obstacles.
notes.ctx: barrier（壁垒）加 breaking（打破）的连字符合成词，一句话概括她从律师到联合国的一路破壁。
notes.ex1: That opportunity began a barrier-breaking career. 那次机会开启了一段破壁的职业生涯。
notes.ex2: She made barrier-breaking achievements in law. 她在法律界取得了破冰式的成就。

notes.en: A laureate is a person who has been given a high official honor, especially the Nobel Prize.
notes.ctx: 拉丁语 laurus 是月桂树，古希腊给优胜者戴月桂花环；Nobel Peace Prize laureate 就是诺奖得主。
notes.ex1: She became a Nobel Peace Prize laureate. 她成为了诺贝尔和平奖得主。
notes.ex2: The laureate gave a moving speech. 桂冠得主发表了动人的演讲。

paragraphs.en_html: In announcing the prize, the Nobel committee said that Ms. Pillay had been “<mark class="voc">instrumental</mark> in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and <mark class="voc">genocide</mark> are <mark class="voc">prosecuted</mark>.” She becomes the fifth South African to win the award, joining the ranks of the country’s most <mark class="voc">vaunted</mark> figures including Nelson Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu.
paragraphs.zh: 宣布奖项时，诺贝尔委员会表示，皮莱“在确保战争罪、危害人类罪与种族灭绝罪得到追诉方面，发挥了关键作用”。她由此成为第五位获此殊荣的南非人，与纳尔逊·曼德拉、德斯蒙德·图图大主教等这个国家最受敬仰的名字，站进了同一列。

notes.en: Instrumental means important in making something happen; playing a key part.
notes.zh: 起关键作用的，功不可没的
notes.ctx: instrument 本义是“工具”，她成了推动这件事最关键的那枚齿轮；比 important 多一层不可替代的功劳。
notes.ex1: She was instrumental in ensuring accountability. 她在确保问责上功不可没。
notes.ex2: His support was instrumental in the project’s success. 他的支持是项目成功的关键。

notes.en: Genocide is the deliberate killing of a whole race or nation of people.
notes.ctx: geno-（希腊语 genos，种族）加 -cide（拉丁语 caedere，杀）；这个词 1944 年由莱姆金创造，他全家死于纳粹之手。
notes.ex1: The tribunal prosecuted crimes of genocide. 该法庭追诉种族灭绝罪。
notes.ex2: Genocide was made a crime after World War Two. 二战后种族灭绝被定为罪行。

notes.en: To prosecute means to officially charge someone with a crime and bring them to court.
notes.ctx: pro-（向前）加 secut（跟随），一路追到底；形近词 persecute 是迫害，只差一个字母，意思天壤之别。
notes.ex1: War criminals were prosecuted after the war. 战犯在战后受到起诉。
notes.ex2: The state decided to prosecute him for fraud. 检方决定以欺诈罪起诉他。

notes.en: Vaunted means praised highly, often publicly.
notes.ctx: 本文取中性偏褒义：南非最受尊崇的名字；只有 much-vaunted 那种说法里才常带“号称厉害其实未必”的讽刺。
notes.ex1: She joined the ranks of the most vaunted figures. 她跻身最受尊崇的人物之列。
notes.ex2: The much-vaunted reform never happened. 那项被吹上天的改革从未兑现。

paragraphs.en_html: While much of Ms. Pillay’s global <mark class="voc">recognition</mark> comes from human rights work she has done abroad, her experiences in South Africa have <mark class="voc">indelibly</mark> shaped her life, and she has remained deeply <mark class="voc">invested</mark> in her home country’s sometimes-<mark class="voc">fragile</mark> democracy. “I see this award as the voice of the majority of the world,” Ms. Pillay said in an interview with the South African state broadcaster on Friday. She added that a majority of South Africans “want <mark class="voc">the rule of law</mark>, they want the independent <mark class="voc">judiciary</mark> to be respected.”
paragraphs.zh: 尽管皮莱享誉全球，多半凭借的是她在海外的人权事业，但真正不可磨灭地塑造了她一生的，是南非这片土地上的经历；而她始终深深牵挂着祖国那尚显稚嫩的民主。“我将这个奖，看作世界多数人的声音，”皮莱周五接受南非国家电视台采访时说。她补充道，大多数南非人“要的是法治，要的是独立的司法体系受到尊重”。

notes.en: Recognition means public praise and reward for someone's work or achievements; also knowing someone or something when you see them.
notes.ctx: 本义是“认出来”，引申为社会认出你的价值；她的这份声誉，大半来自南非之外的人权工作。
notes.ex1: Her work gained international recognition. 她的工作获得了国际认可。
notes.ex2: He was given an award in recognition of his service. 他因贡献卓著获颁奖章。

notes.en: Indelibly means in a way that cannot be erased or removed.
notes.ctx: in-（否定）加 del（涂抹，编辑批注里的 del. 至今还在用）加 -ible；indelible ink 就是投票后三天洗不掉的墨水。
notes.ex1: Her childhood indelibly shaped her life. 她的童年不可磨灭地塑造了她的一生。
notes.ex2: The trip left an indelible impression. 那次旅行留下了不可磨灭的印象。

notes.en: Be deeply invested in something means to care a lot about it and be personally committed to it.
notes.zh: 深度投入的，深切在乎的
notes.ctx: 熟词僻义：不是“投资”，是情感与心力的持续投入——她对祖国那套时好时坏的民主，一直放不下。
notes.ex1: She remained deeply invested in her home country. 她对祖国始终保持深度关切。
notes.ex2: Parents are heavily invested in their children’s education. 家长们在子女教育上倾注极深。

notes.en: Fragile means easily broken or damaged; weak and uncertain.
notes.ctx: 词根 frag- 是打碎（fragment 碎片、fracture 骨折）；sometimes-fragile 说明这民主不是一直脆弱，而是时好时坏。
notes.ex1: The country’s democracy remains fragile. 这个国家的民主仍然脆弱。
notes.ex2: Be careful with that fragile vase. 小心那只易碎的花瓶。

notes.en: The rule of law is the principle that everyone and every institution is equally subject to the law.
notes.ctx: 法律至上、任何人和机构都受其约束；与 rule by law（把法律当治理工具）完全不是一回事。
notes.ex1: Citizens want the rule of law to be respected. 公民希望法治受到尊重。
notes.ex2: The country is rebuilding the rule of law. 这个国家正在重建法治。

notes.en: The judiciary is the branch of government that runs the courts and judges.
notes.ctx: judge 到 judicial（司法的）再到 judiciary（司法机关）；她要的是这套系统不被政治拿捏。
notes.ex1: They demand an independent judiciary. 他们要求司法独立。
notes.ex2: The judiciary must remain free of politics. 司法必须远离政治。

paragraphs.en_html: She studied law at what is now the University of KwaZulu-Natal. Because it was <mark class="voc">segregated</mark>, Black students had to attend classes at night, said Jessica Neuwirth, a human-rights lawyer and activist who has known Ms. Pillay for four decades. During the day, Ms. Pillay would go to the library, where she found books about the <mark class="voc">Nuremberg trials</mark>, helping inspire her <mark class="voc">fascination</mark> with international justice, Ms. Neuwirth said.
paragraphs.zh: 她攻读法律的地方，是如今名为夸祖鲁-纳塔尔大学的学府。据相识皮莱四十载的人权律师、活动家杰西卡·纽沃斯回忆：彼时学校实行种族隔离，非白人学生只能入夜上课。于是白天，皮莱便整日泡在图书馆——正是在那里，她读到了纽伦堡审判的卷宗，也正是这些书，点燃了她对国际正义毕生的着迷。

notes.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people from others, especially by race.
notes.ctx: se-（分开）加 greg（群）；学校被隔离，黑人学生只能夜里上课，白天反而空出一整段时间给她读书。
notes.ex1: Black students had to attend segregated schools. 黑人学生只能上被隔离的学校。
notes.ex2: The city once segregated its beaches by race. 这座城市曾按种族隔离海滩。

notes.en: The Nuremberg trials were the military tribunals held after World War Two to prosecute Nazi war crimes.
notes.ctx: 1945 至 1946 年对纳粹战犯的国际审判，首次确立战争罪与反人类罪，是现代国际刑法的起点，也是全文埋得最深的伏笔。
notes.ex1: The Nuremberg trials created the crime of crimes against humanity. 纽伦堡审判确立了反人类罪。
notes.ex2: She read about the Nuremberg trials as a student. 学生时代她读到了纽伦堡审判。

notes.en: Fascination is a very strong interest in something that holds your attention completely.
notes.ctx: 词源拉丁语 fascinum 意为“巫术、邪眼”，被看住就挪不开眼；她对国际司法的痴迷，始于图书馆的一个白天。
notes.ex1: Her fascination with international justice began in a library. 她对国际司法的痴迷始于图书馆。
notes.ex2: The sea holds a lifelong fascination for him. 大海让他着迷了一辈子。
